price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (>=1 Primary Organizer, Shaper, Terminal Scorer on the floor)
role categories from usage x residual structural influence
talent control / separability from talent and counts
play-type and initiator labels from the possession graph
methodological_questions: Does coverage vary within team beyond what random assignment of players to lineups produces?
Is coverage separable from lineup talent and from role or usage counts, given that roles are built from usage and residual influence?
Does the talent control behave (stable, monotone, not collinear with coverage, not changing sign across specifications)?
Are role labels reliable enough, season to season and split-half, to define coverage?
Is there enough lineup exposure per team-season?

historical_evidence.finding: A flat, non-decaying cross-possession lift collapsed under a within-team baseline and was attributed to a team-quality confound (915,570 possessions; FAIL decay-sanity). Large n gave p~0 with Cohen d of only ~0.01-0.03.
Play-type profile similarity between teammates did not separate absorption from cascade (Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed). Recorded failure type is a powered null, with label-error risk.
Star-suppression gaps were reported with no placebo or matching. The record says later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Defensive scheme labels from NBA matchup/play-by-play fields reached only 14.9% and 3.3% confident-label rates. Label-error and small-sample limits are recorded.
Inferred labels were consistent with label noise (near-uniform transition matrices). Real change could not be separated from the offense executing differently.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID gaps were positive, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. Small-sample limits are recorded.
Player-level gaps came from small n with no multiplicity or clustered test and mixed signs for stars. The record lists placebo-dependence risk.
Counter rankings were unstable across population, team and matchup levels, with sparse cells (n_mu as low as 5). Mechanical-floor and sample-size risks are recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled effect read without a within-team baseline
failed_approaches.why: Team-quality confound; the effect collapsed within team (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Profile similarity used as a separator
failed_approaches.why: It did not separate the outcomes and was almost always findable (B_powered_null, label-error risk).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Descriptive gaps with no placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Placebo dependence; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labels inferred from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Low confident-label rates (14.9% and 3.3%) and small samples (A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Small-n player cells ranked with no multiplicity control
failed_approaches.why: Small n, no multiplicity or clustered test.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage directly. The retrieved work covers play-type, suppression and counter questions.
Within-team baselines and placebo or matched controls are needed because pooled associations in this project have turned out to be team-quality artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Labels inferred from play-by-play can be noisy enough to make questions unanswerable (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
Small player or lineup cells are a recurring limit (FAM:SF-APPS-036, FAM:SF-APPA-048, FAM:SF-APPM-055).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether role coverage varies within team beyond chance.
Whether coverage is separable from talent and usage counts.
How reliable the Organizer/Shaper/Terminal labels are across seasons or splits.
How any talent control behaves. No retrieved record describes one.
own_inferences: The glossary defines roles by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (beyond what usage predicts). Coverage is therefore partly mechanical in usage. A median split forces a share of rotation players into the high-usage roles, and lineup coverage will correlate with summed usage or minutes. Separability from counts must be tested against a permutation null, not assumed.
Roles from rotation medians are unstable for borderline players. Lineup coverage inherits that noise, and some within-team variation may be label flipping.
Most 5-man lineups have small exposure, so the analysis should use minutes-weighted lineup-possession cells or stints with a minimum-exposure gate and cluster by team-season.
If roles are estimated on the full season, early-season lineups use information from later games. A look-ahead-free or split-half role definition is needed.

'Talent control behaves' is undefined in the question. It needs a pre-specified operational meaning: external, out-of-sample, stable under specification changes, and not circular with the usage that defines the roles.
uncertainties: The data description lists 90 team-seasons although the date range suggests more seasons; the exact composition is unclear.
The talent metric, role-assignment window and role-flip rate are unspecified.
The number of lineups with adequate exposure is unknown.
The 2025-26 data were partial before the stated completion dates.
No retrieved record has a recorded validation status.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records contain no direct test of lineup coverage. They did push the design toward within-team baselines, permutation or placebo nulls, label-reliability gates and small-cell exposure gates, and toward not reading pooled effects as findings. They moved the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes.

blocking_constraints.text: Roles are defined from usage and residual influence, so coverage is partly built from usage counts. Separability can only be shown against a permutation null that preserves lineup minutes and role counts.
Role labels (median split, residual influence) may be unstable. If split-half role agreement is low, coverage is not a usable construct.
Many 5-man lineups have too few possessions, so within-team variation may be mostly sampling noise.

prior_work.summary: The retrieved families do not address lineup role coverage. They supply only methodological cautions about team-quality confounds, label noise, small cells and the need for placebo or within-team controls.

risks.text: Coverage is mechanically tied to summed usage and to the number of high-usage players on the floor. With median-split roles and 5 players, 'at least one of each' may be near-saturated for high-minute lineups.
Coverage correlates with talent, minutes, starter status and team quality. Pooled associations have failed before (FAM:SF-CHT-029); the design needs team-season fixed effects.
Role labels near the median or zero-residual boundary flip across splits and seasons, and the talent proxy has its own noise.
Roles and talent estimated on the same games as the lineups, or on the full season, leak future information.
Roles come from possession-level initiations and points. If the talent control or any later outcome uses the same possessions, separability is circular.
Most 5-man lineups have few possessions, so lineup-level variance is dominated by sampling noise unless a minimum-possession gate and shrinkage are used.
With 90 team-seasons, team-level or between-team inferences have limited power even though possessions number 420,993. Cluster by team-season.
Initiator and play-type labels are rule-based inferences from play-by-play. Earlier label inference had low confident-label rates (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Many specifications (talent proxies, thresholds, regular season vs playoffs, seasons) invite forking paths. Pre-specify one primary test.
Rotation patterns differ between regular season and playoffs and across seasons, and in-season roster changes shift role medians.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified quantities: (1) the within-team-season share of variance in a lineup coverage indicator (and a 0-3 count of covered roles) beyond a permutation null; (2) the partial association of coverage with lineup talent after team-season fixed effects, usage sum and role counts, summarised as the incremental R^2 of coverage over talent and counts; (3) behaviour of the talent control, defined as split-half reliability, monotone and stable slope, and VIF with coverage.
design.unit: Lineup cell (same 5 players), possession-weighted, within team-season. Roles are assigned per player-season, with a split-half robustness check.
design.sample: All available team-seasons from 2022-23 to 2024-25 plus complete 2025-26 regular seasons (playoffs analysed separately). Exclude garbage time. Include lineup cells with at least 50 possessions (sensitivity gates at 25 and 100). Confirm the actual team-season count (90 recorded) before analysis.
design.power: Primary power is at the team-season level (about 90 clusters). Detect a within-team variance share beyond the permutation null and an incremental R^2 of about 0.02 using cluster bootstrap CIs. Pre-state the minimum number of eligible lineup cells. If fewer than about 10 eligible cells per team-season are available on average, report the result as untestable, not as a null.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects. Out-of-sample talent proxy (prior-season or odd-even split-half player rating, not from the same possessions that define roles). Lineup minutes or possessions, summed usage, starter share and number of high-usage players. Roles from odd games applied to even-game lineups, and the reverse. Report role-label split-half agreement (kappa) and require at least moderate agreement (kappa >= 0.4) for the construct to be usable.
design.falsification: (a) Permutation null: shuffle role labels among players within team-season, keeping each player's minutes and usage, and recompute coverage. (b) Shuffle lineup membership among stints within team-season. (c) Placebo role definition: a usage-only median split with no residual influence, to check whether the findings reflect usage rather than structure. (d) Talent control sanity: monotone and stable dose-response in split halves and no sign flip when the proxy is swapped. Failure of any check means the result is classed as an artifact, not support.
design.multiplicity: One primary test per estimand (three in total), with Holm correction across them. All other cuts (season, regular season vs playoffs, gates) are labelled secondary and reported with FDR control. Thresholds and the talent proxy are fixed before analysis.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (1) the within-team variance share exceeds the permutation null (95% CI excludes 0), (2) incremental R^2 of coverage over talent and counts is at least 0.02 with the CI excluding 0, (3) the talent control passes the split-half stability and no-sign-flip checks, and (4) the placebo usage-only definition does not reproduce the result. Rejected if the CIs exclude the above thresholds with adequate exposure. Untestable if role reliability or lineup exposure fails the pre-set gates. Artifact if the result vanishes under any falsification check.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived possession graph, with 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 and playoffs from 2026-06-21. Freeze a data snapshot, record the version, and run only on the frozen snapshot; use the stated date of 2026-07-13 as the data cut-off.

research_concepts: role classification from play-type possession records
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and usage counts?
Does within-team variation in coverage exist beyond sampling noise?
Does the talent control behave as expected (monotone, stable, not collinear with coverage)?
How reliable are role labels derived from play-by-play and play-type possessions?
Sample size and exposure sparsity of lineups across 90 team-seasons
args.query: lineup coverage organizer shaper terminal roles within-team variation separable from talent and counts, talent control behavior

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

TOOL_RESULT glossary:
# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.

- **Possession, PPP:** a team's continuous spell with the ball; PPP is points per possession.
- **H1, H2:** first half (periods 1 and 2) and second half (periods 3 and 4) of a game. RS and PO: regular season and playoffs.
- **Play type:** the label assigned to each possession by the project's rule-based classifier from play-by-play events. Labels include PNR (pick-and-roll ball handler), DRIVE, CUT, SPOT_UP, PULL_UP, POST_UP, PUTBACK and TRANSITION. A play-type mix is a team's share of possessions in each play type.
- **Initiator, initiation:** the offensive player whose action starts the possession's play type (for example the cutter on a cut, the ball handler on a pick-and-roll). Initiation records are possession-level rows linking initiator, play type and points.
- **Inferrer:** the classifier step that infers a play type (for example a pick-and-roll) from play-by-play text when it is not recorded directly.
- **Suppression trigger:** a team, play type and game in which the team's PPP on that play type falls sharply from H1 to H2 under fixed minimum-attempt rules; read as the defense possibly taking the action away.
- **Continuation, counter:** after a trigger, continuation means the offense keeps running the triggered play type; a counter is a different play type run instead.
- **BEST, AVOID (counter tiers):** the strategy app's matchup-ranked counter recommendations after a trigger. BEST is the top-ranked counter play type for that matchup, AVOID the lowest-ranked.
- **Structural fingerprint:** a team's standardized pattern of how play types share initiators.
- **Structural influence (load, L):** how much a team's structural fingerprint changes when one player's initiations are removed. L_pre is that quantity measured from games before an absence.
- **Usage:** a player's share of team possessions he initiates or finishes.
- **Role categories (Structural Influence paper):** by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (structural influence beyond what usage predicts): Primary Organizer (high usage, positive residual), Shaper (low usage, positive residual), Terminal Scorer (high usage, residual at or below zero), Role Occupant or Specialist (low usage, residual at or below zero).
- **Connector:** a structural-role label used in later studies for players whose presence links teammates' play types; the exact rule varied between studies.
- **Hub:** a high-structural-influence player around whom a team's initiations are organized.
- **Absence spell:** a run of consecutive games a player misses (the main studies used at least 15).
- **Displacement (D_real):** how far teammates' play-type mix moves during an absence spell relative to before it (one minus the cosine similarity of the two mixes).
- **Mover, decoy:** a mover is a player who changed teams between seasons; decoys are comparison players used as placebo matches for a mover.
- **Stint:** an interval of play with the same ten players on the court.
- **Garbage time:** late-game possessions with a lopsided score, usually excluded.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm settling on the roles now: each is set by usage combined with residual influence, meaning the influence left over after predicting from usage. Coverage means the lineup has at least one of each. I'm also noticing that defining roles from usage makes the "separable from talent" claim partly mechanical, since the cutoff sits at the rotation median and the residual is orthogonal to usage by construction. Terminal players are the high-usage ones with residual at or below zero, and I'm checking coverage of all three across the lineup.

I'm checking whether the circularity matters, since the roles are derived from the same possessions used to measure lineup outcomes. I also want to see whether all three roles show up across a typical five-man lineup under the median split.

I'm laying out the design now: compare within-team variance in lineup coverage against a permutation null that shuffles players among lineups while keeping minutes fixed, and test its separability using talent proxies built from out-of-sample splits. I'm setting the bar at stable coefficients, no sign flips, and variance inflation under 5. I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes, with the main risk being a mechanical floor from usage-based role definitions.

I'm now working out the risk list: mechanical floor, confounding, measurement reliability, power, exposure sparsity, and leakage from using full-season roles on early lineups. I also need to check the label-error and multiple-testing risks, and keep the risk codes valid. Then I'll write the output with the historical evidence status exactly as recorded.
